IPS touch display and speaker; USB-C charging. January 2022 charging guide specifies 5 V/3 A input for its recommended 15 W charging setup, not a 5 V battery.
Rubberized wheels and rechargeable power. Product page estimates roughly four hours charging at 15 W; operating duration depends on use.
Wi-Fi connection through the Miko parent application; the reviewed setup instructions do not identify radio chip or RF band.

facts.details: LTE antenna and cellular connection; modem model and operating bands unspecified.

Manufacturer lists 25.9 V, 60 Ah and approximately 1,500 Wh; charger output 29.4 V/6 A. Four-wheel drive, independent double-wishbone suspension and skid steering; 20 kg safe payload, 61.5 kg unladen.

Camera eyes, microphones, touch sensing, IMUs, 3D camera, FLIR, surrounding cameras, time-of-flight and proximity sensors; navigation base includes LiDAR.
32 facial degrees of freedom; articulated neck, arms/hands, torso and spine. Diagram marks legs optional and describes self-charging mobility with emergency bumpers; battery capacity unspecified.
Speaker, microphone array and touch-sensitive face, shoulders, arms and hands.
Hanson-AI language/motion processing and SLAM navigation; navigation/control modules vary by ordered configuration.

Four chassis cameras, two on the manipulator, and optional mast camera; day/night imagery, near-IR illumination and two-way audio. Arm includes 30× optical-zoom autofocus and close-range gripper cameras.

ROCU external controller; onboard computer and operating-system details are not given.

profiles.configuration: RT-1000/PROBOT manufacturer sheet in the August 2025 publication path. Brochure configuration; newer website weights and dimensions differ. CPU, memory, battery capacity and radio chip are not disclosed.

facts.details: Secure IP mobile ad-hoc network; stated standard-gear line-of-sight reach up to 1 km is a manufacturer claim, not a guaranteed detection radius.
360-degree day/night video, near-IR illumination and GPS waypoint navigation. Camera and GNSS part numbers unspecified.
Nominal 48 V rechargeable batteries, eight-hour stated operation; 750 kg payload and 8 km/h brochure speed.
External power, Ethernet RJ45, 24 V output, GPS/RF antenna and communication connections.
Dedicated joystick and external ROCU-7 control/display unit; follow-me kit and GPS waypoint modes. Controller hardware is not an onboard CPU identification.

profiles.configuration: Current Otter manufacturer specification, separate from Mariner X and customer-modified research craft. Embedded processor, RAM, storage and battery-pack SKU undisclosed.

facts.details: 5 GHz MIMO radio/Wi-Fi; MBR, VHF and 4G are additional options.
Camera and Class B AIS; optional SeaSight enhanced perception. Survey sonar and other payloads depend on configuration.
Two electric thrusters and up to four interchangeable battery packs; up to 20 hours at 2 knots, dependent on load and conditions. Published dry weight 62 kg and payload 30 kg.
Modular hull and plug-and-play payload mounting; subsystems can be separated into units under 20 kg for transport.
Vehicle Control Station provides waypoint/course/heading control and live sensor views; rugged-laptop control and mobile manual-control app. SeaCapture data software is optional.

profiles.configuration: Mariner X manufacturer specification. This larger vessel is distinct from Otter. CPU, memory, engine, battery and modem part numbers are not stated.

facts.details: LTE/4G standard high-bandwidth link; MBR and Starlink optional.
GNSS compass, cameras, radar and Class B AIS; SeaSight, Class A AIS and VHF are optional upgrades.

Redundant propulsion, bow thrusters and temperature-controlled equipment space/radome. Published 5,000 kg dry weight, 1,200 kg payload, up to 12 knots and up to 25 days endurance depend on configuration.
Railed aft deck, two moonpool elevators and two dedicated sensor positions. Winches, generators and vehicle launch/recovery equipment are selectable payloads.
Maritime Robotics Autonomous Navigation System supports remote/autonomous navigation and coordinated vessel operation. SeaCapture is optional.

profiles.configuration: NTNU Fish Otter research modification: hardware notes dated March 2021, navigation notes February 2020 and software page January 2025. Not the factory specification or a Mariner X configuration. Storage and exact radio-band setup unspecified.

facts.details: Raspberry Pi 4 with GPIO-connected Strato Pi CAN board and independent hardware watchdog; CAN links the Torqeedo interface board.
4 GB RAM on the Raspberry Pi 4.
BulletAC IP67 radio powered by passive PoE; no vehicle-specific MAC asserted.
Hemisphere V104s dual-GPS heading/position receiver with gyro and tilt sensors; RS-232 through USB adapter and PPS. Control box supports TBR-700-/RT hydrophone via a SLIM RS-485 board.
Two Torqeedo Ultralight 403 thrusters; four replaceable Torqeedo packs totaling 3,660 Wh/124 Ah in the documented build.
CAN, GPIO, RS-485 hydrophone interface, serial-to-USB navigation link and passive PoE radio power.
Customized DUNE on Ubuntu Server 20.04, Neptus operator console and IMC messaging from the LSTS toolchain.

facts.component: Wave propulsion and solar electrical power
facts.details: SV3: up to 6.8 kWh/225 W solar; SV5: 15.7 kWh/525 W; SV6: 30 kWh/900 W. SV6 introduces native 48 V payload support. These are maxima, not every installation.
SV3/SV5/SV6 respectively: 7/21/40 modular bays and maximum 70/215/450 kg payload. Floats measure 3.05/5.15/5.6 m.

Sensor payloads mount on the mast, float or submerged body, or are towed/cast; WHOI configuration relays underwater-vehicle acoustic messages.

WGMS provides fleet health, waypoint control and data access; deployment options include commercial/government cloud or on-premises infrastructure. WHOI’s SV3 Block II identifies onboard Regulus software.

profiles.configuration: Manufacturer identifies Guardian as the successor name to Solus-XR. Battery and hydrogen configurations are separate. CPU, memory, modem and sensor part numbers are not disclosed; publication gives conflicting fuel-cell endurance figures.

facts.details: Lithium-ion battery variant: 480 hours/2,650 km published. Hydrogen fuel-cell variant: 925 hours/5,000 km in the specification table; headline says over 45 days, so no single reconciled endurance is asserted. Redundant propellers and hover/station-keeping capability.
11.7 m long, 1.66 m wide/high. Two 1.2 × 1.2 × 1.7 m payload bays or a single bay; retractable communication/sensor mast. Depth-rating options are 300, 1,000 or 3,000 m.
Mission-specific sensor payloads; optional pipe/cable tracking and terrain/feature navigation. Towed arrays and off-platform equipment are options, not baseline fit.
Manufacturer describes satellite reporting through the mast; radio/modem type and bands are not specified.
Adaptive mission planning and optional third-party autonomy packages; operating system unspecified.

facts.details: Thermal night-vision camera capability; sensor models undisclosed.
Rapid battery exchange; 2.5-hour charging claim, 40 km travel range, 15 km/h maximum speed and up to 500 kg load. Published 72-hour operating time is not 72 hours of continuous maximum-speed driving.
Tool-free ARX payload interfaces support configurable logistics, inspection and other applications.
Manufacturer states up to 4 km control range but does not disclose RF band or radio module; range is not a scanner identification.
Manual and supervised autonomous operation; ARX describes the GEREON fleet as using the ARX Robotics Framework with Mithra OS, linking sensors, autonomy and open interfaces.

Five Intel RealSense D435i RGB-D cameras: four at the base and one in the forehead, plus a stereo eye pair. Joint torque and balance sensing are also documented by DLR.
WLAN and wired Ethernet connect external operators; frequency and module part number unspecified.
Ethernet sensor transport and EtherCAT real-time control; sensor management distributed across head and base.
Debian 9 on Hannibal; Debian 9 PREEMPT_RT on Face; QNX on Amit; Jetson OS on sensor modules. DLR Links and Nodes coordinates software processes.
DLR lists 51 degrees of freedom, approximately 200 kg, 20 kg nominal load and battery operation exceeding 60 minutes; battery voltage/capacity unspecified.

15 Ah / 0.72 kWh battery. Published body: 170 cm, 65 kg, 42 degrees of freedom and 352 Nm maximum joint torque.

14 planetary roller-screw and 14 rotary actuators; 175 cm, 75 kg. Manufacturer claims eight-hour operation after one-hour charging; test conditions and battery chemistry unspecified.
Two 11-DOF hands using 12 coreless motors in total; wrist force sensing and 25 tactile points per finger described. Presentation lists 25–30 kg dual-arm carrying and 15 kg single-hand load.
Layered perception/decision/control with vision, voice and touch fusion. Nebula embodied software supports modular programming, simulation, multi-robot coordination, debugging and OTA updates.

ROSA 2.0 robotic application framework, semantic VSLAM, language-model task planning and learned whole-body motion control. Supports coordinated manufacturing workflows with AMRs/AGVs.

95 cm arm reach; 7.5 kg per arm/15 kg combined. Mechanical/vacuum grippers or humanoid hands. Teach pendant and Oculus Rift remote-guidance options.
Perception, reasoning, interaction and navigation modules; graph-based mission authoring and fleet management. ERP/MES integration and telemetry are documented.

facts.details: Wi-Fi 6 and 5G-ready capability; no module or network identifier published.
3D laser/LiDAR, depth cameras, force feedback, cardioid microphone, 60 W speakers and touch display.

180 cm/150 kg; 70 cm reach, six axes per arm and 5 kg per-arm/10 kg combined load. Grippers, vacuum tools and humanoid hands are configuration choices.
Multimodal mission and navigation software, fleet management, graph-based workflows and clinical-system integration. Remote guidance via pendant/Oculus Rift.

profiles.configuration: RoBee Series F October 2025 manufacturer datasheet. Distinct intralogistics platform; processor, RAM, storage, battery capacity and radio module are undisclosed.

facts.details: Wi-Fi 6; advertised 5G-ready capability does not establish an active cellular installation.
Eight cameras including depth and wrist-mounted vision, LiDAR, encoders and force feedback; cardioid microphone and 60 W speakers.
Six batteries; manufacturer lists lithium-ion plus graphene supercapacitor energy storage. Up to eight hours typical operation, 230 V AC supply; omnidirectional base, maximum 0.6 m/s.
Seven-axis arms on vertically moving, rotating pneumatic support; 120 cm reach, 10 kg per arm/20 kg combined. Rear module carries up to 500 kg; complete robot weighs 850 kg.
MES/WMS/industrial-IoT connections, cloud fleet monitoring, autonomous route planning and front touchscreen/voicebot interface.

profiles.configuration: Intel CES January 2026 demonstration only; not proof that all RoBee R/M/F units contain this processor. Exact SKU, memory and storage are not given.

facts.details: Intel Core Ultra Series 3 edge processor family identified by Intel for the showcased RoBee. Exact chip SKU undisclosed.
Demonstrated speech recognition/generation, reasoning and selected vision tasks run onboard. This demo claim does not mean every RoBee product lacks cloud services.

profiles.configuration: February/March 2024 engineering articles describe the 12 m telescoping-tower generation, not the redesigned 2026 platform. Processor SKUs, memory, battery chemistry/capacity and radio hardware undisclosed.

facts.details: Central base computer plus separate computers on each scanning rail process images locally. Sensor timestamps are synchronized centrally; Ethernet links the rail computers to the base.
Tower: 17 cameras, 17 lights and two LiDAR units. Base: four LiDAR units, two cameras and further perception sensors. Sensor models unspecified.

Multiple rechargeable batteries provide approximately 4–5 scanning hours; under-three-hour recharge and automatic dock return. Six-wheel base uses two central driven wheels and front/rear wheel pairs on pivoting arms.
Six linked telescoping sections, 3 m collapsed/12 m extended, with camera coverage of racks up to 14 m. Rope/pulley winch lifts rails; Ethernet harnesses run in drag chains.
Wi-Fi connectivity sends filtered results to the cloud; robot processing accommodates intermittent connectivity. Wi-Fi standard and module unspecified.
Camera/LiDAR localization, barcode and volume processing happen onboard before reduced datasets feed DexoryView digital twins; remote software updates supported.

profiles.configuration: Aethon-authored 2016 T3 datasheet, specification 293130, mirrored by its distributor. Not every TUG generation. CPU, RAM, storage, radio module and battery voltage/capacity unspecified.

facts.details: Wi-Fi or 900 MHz option; no exact protocol, channel or unique signature given.
Multiple LiDAR, sonar and infrared sensors; indoor-map localization without added navigation markers.
Valve-regulated lead-acid batteries; ten-hour advertised operation with intermittent charging. Automatic docking/charging and omnidirectional four-wheel drive; 453 kg maximum carrying capacity.
Automatic cart pickup/drop-off; touchscreen, handheld, scheduled, multi-stop and manufacturing-system dispatch options.
Local hosting or remote Aethon Command Center over an encrypted VPN; onboard operating system not specified.

Wi-Fi and Bluetooth recorded in the field study; radio chips, versions and broadcast identifiers are not specified.
Battery-powered tracked carriage with vertical lift. Hilti advertises up to eight hours between charges; battery chemistry and electrical capacity are not given here.
Study configuration uses Hilti TE-6A drill and VC-75 dust extractor, external PLC 400 tablet and joystick controller. Operator moves it between drilling zones.
AutoCAD/Revit plans pass through Hilti Cloud to the PLC 400; total-station registration guides automatic drilling within the work area. Progress synchronizes back to the project system.

profiles.configuration: Manufacturer V5 datasheet dated June 5, 2026 and current product page. CPU/GPU, RAM, storage, battery chemistry/capacity and radio module are not specified. Not the older Gen 3 specification.

facts.details: LiDAR, RGB camera/webcam, infrared, ultrasonic, GPS and environmental temperature/humidity sensors. Manufacturer describes 360-degree perception and touchless human detection to three metres.
Wi-Fi and Bluetooth; radio versions, chipsets and broadcast identifiers are not identified.
Actuated wheels and a linear axis; advertised motion endurance 2–8 hours with automatic recharging. Battery capacity and test duty cycle are not disclosed.

17 base-robot degrees of freedom excluding end effectors; 3 kg single-arm payload. Touch display, projector, microphone array, amplifier/speakers and LEDs; modular shelf, table, hook and tool-change attachments.

Neuraverse no-code applications, fleet deployment and digital-twin simulation; NEURA Gym training. SLAM navigation, path planning, computer vision and language-model interaction; developer API access advertised.

profiles.configuration: August 2024 launch configuration, not Figure 03 or later Helix revisions. NVIDIA names RTX-based modules but not GPU SKU, CPU, RAM or storage; radio hardware and battery chemistry are undisclosed.

facts.details: Two NVIDIA RTX GPU-based modules; NVIDIA attributes a threefold inference gain over the first-generation robot to adding the second module. No specific RTX or Jetson model established.
Six onboard RGB cameras, microphones and speakers; sensor part numbers unspecified.
Custom 2.25 kWh battery pack inside the torso. Launch release gives energy capacity, not a tested operating-hour rating.
Fourth-generation hands have 16 degrees of freedom each. Power and compute cables are routed inside the structure; connector and actuator SKUs are not published.

Onboard vision-language reasoning; launch speech models developed with OpenAI. NVIDIA Isaac Sim/Omniverse and off-robot NVIDIA GPUs support simulation and training; these are not additional onboard modules.

profiles.configuration: TI September 2024 Proteus component disclosure, with Amazon/AWS autonomy description. Not every Amazon mobile robot or the newer natural-language Proteus revision. Installed RAM, storage, radio, battery and camera/LiDAR SKUs undisclosed.

facts.details: TI identifies TDA4VM and DRA821 embedded processors, with an RM46L852 safety microcontroller supporting the TDA4VM in Proteus.
TI lists dual Arm Cortex-A72, six Cortex-R5F cores, C7x and C66x DSPs, a vision accelerator and PowerVR GPU for this SoC. Chip capabilities do not establish robot clock settings or enabled functions.
Vision and object classification maintain a protective boundary around people; Amazon/AWS also documents LiDAR and 3D point-cloud navigation.
TI documents Ethernet, CAN and RS-485 connectivity solutions in the robot design. These are internal/system interfaces, not passive wireless identifiers.
TI power-management ICs accompany the embedded processors. Exact PMIC SKU, battery chemistry and capacity are not disclosed.
Embedded diagnostics support safe rerouting or shutdown; Amazon SageMaker supports development of perception models. This is separate from the onboard processors that execute robot control.

profiles.configuration: Amazon’s published Hercules mobile-drive architecture. CPU, memory, storage, radio module, battery specification and actuator models are not disclosed. Do not inherit Proteus chips.

facts.details: Forward-facing 3D camera recognizes people, shelves and obstacles; camera-readable floor markers support localization and pod finding.
Amazon documents locating employees through Wi-Fi Tech Vest transmitters. No exact radio module, channel or device-specific beacon pattern is given.
Wheeled drive slides below a storage pod and lifts it for transport; published capacity up to 1,250 lb. Electrical ratings and charging hardware unspecified.
Local movement decisions operate under centralized order-driven fleet planning; safety responses include electrical-power loss.

profiles.configuration: Amazon’s November 2023 Titan launch architecture. Component reuse is documented at subsystem level only: no CPU, RAM, storage, radio or battery capacity can be inferred from other robots.

facts.details: Uses hardware components from Proteus to support operating-system execution, planning and interfaces. Amazon does not identify which chips are shared.
Computer vision and obstacle-detection systems are derived from Xanthus; exact camera and sensor models undisclosed.
Reuses the Hercules battery/charging-management solution; maximum load 2,500 lb. Battery energy, motor and charger ratings unspecified.
Xanthus-derived user controls and interfaces to other fulfillment-center systems; port and protocol details not published.
Mobile transport of large-item storage loads under Amazon’s fulfillment workflows. Operating-system name and version undisclosed.

profiles.configuration: Next-generation Skypod introduced February 2025; manufacturer specifications and integrator Klinkhammer’s 2025 brochure. CPU, memory, storage, radio hardware and battery capacity undisclosed.

facts.details: Laser scanner for obstacle detection; scanner manufacturer and model not specified.
Four-wheel drive, maximum 4 m/s and rack climbing to 14 m. Lithium battery with booster opportunity charging; integrator specifies about five charging minutes per operating hour.
30 kg payload; standard Exotec bins/trays or customer containers. Robot interfaces with racks, picking workstations and automatic Exchangers.
Central route coordination, order buffering, sequencing and pick-and-pack integration. Redesigned robot-to-robot picking workstations are part of the 2025 system.

profiles.configuration: Anduril-authored 2022 Australian product sheet, publicly mirrored by Second Line of Defense. Not Dive-XL/Ghost Shark. Processor, memory, battery chemistry, navigation sensor models and wireless/acoustic modem are not specified.

facts.details: 93 kWh stated energy capacity; four days at 4 knots with SAS survey payload, versus ten days at 2.5 knots without payload. Published 2022 mass 2,700 kg; 5.8 m long and 1.2 m diameter.
Ethernet, RS-232, RS-485 and RS-422. More than one cubic metre payload volume and open software/mechanical/electrical interfaces; wired ports do not establish an RF signature.

Options include side-scan/synthetic-aperture sonar, sub-bottom profiler, multibeam echo sounder, magnetometer and cameras. Up to five payloads can be integrated; none is asserted as universal equipment.
Planned autonomous missions can execute without continuous communication or human intervention, returning to a pier or vessel. Current product page retains modular open-interface design.

Wheeled humanoid rated 192 lb, 33 lb carrying capacity and 9 mph maximum speed. Manufacturer advertises up to six hours of operation after one hour charging; battery chemistry and motor SKU unspecified.

profiles.configuration: 2018 SICK/6 River supplier case study, 2020 manufacturer brochure and 2022 FES architecture. Historical configuration; newer revisions may differ. CPU, RAM, storage, radio module and battery chemistry/capacity undisclosed.

facts.details: SICK TiM-family LiDAR uses surrounding contours for navigation; exact TiM SKU unspecified. A mounted product scanner reads item, lot and serial information.
Tablet-sized task display; TiM sensors include Ethernet. Brochure documents scanning and put-to-light workflows, with up to six shelf levels.
Battery management requests automatic charging. 2020 brochure rates payload at 90.7 kg and advertises three shifts from one hour of charging without defining shift length or battery energy.
Onboard control and workflows connect with cloud services and The Bridge operator console; warehouse-management integrations coordinate allocation and routes.

profiles.configuration: Manufacturer’s security-service configuration. CPU/GPU, RAM, storage, battery capacity and radio module are not published here. Research-platform Jetson, battery and camera specifications are not assigned to Guard.

facts.details: Thermal, RGB and infrared cameras support patrol observations; exact sensors, lens specifications and resolution unspecified.
Autonomous charging with advertised battery life exceeding eight hours. Manufacturer describes all-weather operation at walking speed; electrical ratings undisclosed.
Web application supports remote robot control and live communication; manufacturer states end-to-end encryption without publishing radio or protocol details.
Scheduled patrols, AI-assisted reports and integration with existing video-management systems.

profiles.configuration: MYBOTSHOP’s configurable Research platform, separate from Ascento Guard. FAQ lists D435f and docking included; current manual lists D435i and optional autonomous docking. These are unresolved package/revision differences. RAM size and storage capacity unspecified.

facts.details: Dedicated NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX system-on-module for user development; memory variant and underlying motion-controller chip are not named.
Livox Mid-360 LiDAR and Fixposition Vision-RTK2 GNSS/INS. Manual also allows Hesai JT16 LiDAR. RealSense D435i appears in the manual, D435f in the FAQ; confirm the supplied configuration.
Steam Deck connects over the robot’s onboard Wi-Fi. Radio chipset and a universal broadcast signature are not established.
50.4 V, 17.5 Ah, 882 Wh battery with 12S5P arrangement; unregulated battery-voltage and 24 V outputs for accessories.
Six driven joints across two legs and wheels; Steam Deck teleoperation. Cable charging is standard in the current manual; autonomous docking depends on package.
ROS 2 Humble, Zenoh bridge and onboard browser dashboard. SLAM is available; odometric/map navigation remains marked under development.

facts.details: 433.2–434.79 MHz, specified output 8.5 dBm. Modulation and radio-chip identity unspecified; frequency alone is not a device signature.
24 V DC operation, 100 W stated consumption; two sealed lead-acid 12 V / 105 Ah batteries. Charging contacts rated 24 V / 25 A.
35 kg payload including bin; up to 3.1 m/s travel and 1.6 m/s lift. Four switches, three LEDs and a local emergency stop; IP20.

35 kg bin-inclusive payload; 220/330 mm bins. Five switches, multicolor status LED, local emergency stop and antenna/status dome.

profiles.configuration: ACWA’s published water-pipe inspection architecture. ST Micro is an electronics supplier reference, not a disclosed CPU SKU. RAM, storage capacity, radio/acoustic modem, battery and actuator models remain unspecified.

facts.details: Proprietary electronics and in-house mission software use ST Micro technologies; exact microcontroller or SoC not disclosed.
Onboard platform stores data from configurable sensors; medium and capacity are not published.

Canaloc combines sensor information for GPS-free pipe mapping. Mission options include residual wall thickness, corrosion, cracks, deformation and water parameters; not every sensor is installed on every robot.
Articulated platform follows bends and branches while water remains flowing; designed for constrained pipes with pressures up to 300 PSI.
In-house embedded mission control and web-based processing associate collected measurements with the reconstructed pipe route.

profiles.configuration: Manufacturer’s TyBOT 3.0 public manual. Not TyBOT 1.5. Processor, RAM, storage, operating system and radio hardware are not identified.

facts.details: Dual cameras on the tram identify intersections; camera sensors and lenses unspecified.
Field-replaceable commercial generator meeting 7,000 W, 60 Hz, 240 VAC requirements. No mandatory generator brand or battery specification is established.
Adjustable legs and bogies run on rails; moving tram positions the tie module. Module uses 15 lb spools of 16.5 AWG coated or 16 AWG black wire.
Supervisor defines work zones through the Belly Box; robot ties detected intersections in selectable patterns. Main panel includes generator disconnect and emergency-stop status.

profiles.configuration: Manufacturer 2025 version 3.0 sheet and product description. CPU, RAM, storage, OS, camera SKU and radio frequency/module undisclosed.

facts.details: Cameras detect rebar capture; local odometry supports repeated placement after the supervisor sets the starting position.
Cummins Onan 7 kW generator, split-phase 240 V / 30 A; 53-gallon tank, 87-octane gasoline. Sheet advertises 50+ hours between refueling and 0.95 gallons/hour at full load.
Tram and slew bearing move/rotate a placement boom. 5,000 lb bundle capacity, 9–60 ft bars and rail spacing 27–117 ft; bogies travel at 0.2 m/s.
Belly Box mobile transmitter provides the supervisor link; no exact radio protocol, channel or chipset specified.
Belly Box supplies spacing, modes, emergency stop and overrides. Manufacturer describes supervised placement without BIM input; it is not claimed to operate unattended.

profiles.configuration: 2024 design-partner Whipsaw disclosures. CPU/GPU, memory, radio, power rating, motor and camera SKU are not published. Describes the massage platform, not an autonomous mobile robot.

facts.details: Four overhead infrared sensors construct a 3D body map; design account also identifies pressure sensing.
Two robotic arms use Aerpoint contact heads with seven shaped surfaces. Touch interface beneath the headrest, integrated audio and safety shutoff support direct user control.
Body mapping and chosen programs guide arm movements; saved user preferences can be reused across Aescape platforms. Cloud/radio implementation details are not disclosed.

profiles.configuration: Published 4AG harvesting architecture. Older harvesting page describes bulk boxes and future punnets; newer homepage promotes Forager HX800 punnet handling. facts.details: Machine vision supports mushroom selection and harvesting; camera model and illumination arrangement unspecified.
Harvesting equipment mounts to existing growing shelves and can be moved between rooms. It performs picking, trimming and packing; destination container depends on model.
Autonomous vision-based harvesting with software updates; collected crop data supports refinements to selection and timing.

profiles.configuration: Origin One 1.0/4 documentation. Sensor and autonomy packages differ: optional LiDAR, RTK and software must be confirmed for the supplied platform. RAM, storage capacity, radio-chip and real-time-controller SKU undisclosed.

facts.details: NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX; memory variant unspecified. Auxiliary CAN/RS485 connect to a separate proprietary real-time controller whose processor is not identified.

Wi-Fi 6 at 2.4/5 GHz, LTE Cat 4 with SIM slot, and Bluetooth 5.2. Electrical guide additionally lists a 2.4 GHz remote-stop antenna and 868 MHz RTK antenna; antenna coverage does not prove an installed radio mode.
Six-axis IMU, magnetometer, four wheel encoders, six ultrasonic sensors and RealSense D435f depth camera. Optional 32-line Ouster LiDAR and RTK-GNSS.
650 Wh / 15 Ah battery; 50.4 V / 5 A charger. Four 166 W motors with holding brakes. Accessory outputs: 12 V and 24 V pairs, each pair limited to 100 W combined; battery-voltage output 200 W.
Gigabit Ethernet and USB 3.0. CAN, RS485 and digital I/O need manufacturer enablement; their presence does not establish public network services.

CreOS Linux manages Docker containers, ROS 2 services and a Zenoh bridge. An optional access point uses a configurable Origin <Serial> name; this is only a candidate naming pattern, not authenticated device identification.

profiles.configuration: ALICE 4 manufacturer configuration; options may vary. Not ALICE M1 or ALICE 5. RAM, storage, battery capacity, radio module and camera model undisclosed.

Stereo depth camera, six-axis IMU and custom foot-contact/FSR sensors.
Proprietary back-drivable linear actuators and dedicated motor drivers. Electrical supply and battery chemistry are not published.
41 degrees of freedom: legs 6 each, waist 1, arms 7 each, head 2 and hands 6 each. Published body: 160 cm, approximately 45 kg.
Real-time field-oriented motor control supports position, velocity, torque and impedance modes. Manufacturer provides a URDF download.

Stereo camera, IMU, 3D LiDAR and laser sensor; exact sensor SKUs not named.
97 kg, adjustable height 1.3–1.8 m. Thirty-one degrees of freedom: waist 3, arms 7 each, head 2 and hands 6 each; dual parallel-link waist.

LiDAR plus front and rear cameras; exact sensor models are not published.

TraXwise planning and monitoring with application control and data gathering. Firmware, controller silicon and wireless protocol unspecified.

profiles.configuration: X3 sheet linked from the SeaExplorer 1000 product page. Not the X2 or 200/Shallow model. CPU part numbers, RAM, storage and battery energy unspecified.

facts.details: Two independent CPUs running Linux, assigned to navigation and payload control.

Legato + CODA CTD/dissolved-oxygen payload is the reference configuration for published endurance, not a guarantee for every sensor package.

GLIMPSE processing/monitoring; survey, virtual mooring, drifting and bottoming modes.

facts.details: Primary and backup satellite WAN, nearshore 4G and UHF remote control. Class A AIS transceiver, dual-watch VHF and NAVTEX are also listed; no modem SKU or unique RF signature established.

14 m aluminium SWATH hull; modular equipment racks, 10/20-foot ISO moonpool and CAN-based controls. ROV, sonar and drone payloads are optional integrations.

Automatic AirDock charging, onboard battery heater and cell balancing; chemistry and capacity not published.
Cargo: advertised 20 km with 5 kg under the winch. Patrol: 35 km with its included payload. These are different test configurations, not interchangeable ratings.

profiles.configuration: Configurable A-Series parcel-sorting cell. Processor, accelerator, memory, power supply, radio and arm/camera models are not named. Do not import B-Series scan-tunnel specifications.

AmbiOS uses simulation-trained grasp planning and vision-based quality checks. Image, video, timing and performance data support operational analysis.

profiles.configuration: Modular B-Series induction/sorting system; pick-cell and destination counts vary. CPU/GPU, RAM, power supply, radio, camera and arm SKUs undisclosed.

Multi-suction gripper and robot arm transfer parcels onto buffer and central conveyors; routing sends items into gaylord containers or a reject bin. Pick cells are configurable.
AmbiOS simulation-trained planning and quality checks. Optional warehouse-management-system integration supplies sort destinations; no public radio signature is established.

profiles.configuration: Original 48 MP/8K EVO II configuration in Autel’s historical specification page; not Pro, Dual or V3. CPU, RAM, flight-controller and radio-chip part numbers undisclosed.

2.4–2.4835 GHz in this configuration; regional transmit-power limits apply. Later EVO II revisions have different radio specifications.
48 MP half-inch CMOS camera, 25.6 mm-equivalent f/1.8 lens and three-axis gimbal; 8K video at 24/25 fps. Six-direction binocular sensing and GPS positioning.
7,100 mAh, 11.55 V, 82 Wh LiPo 3S battery, 365 g. Advertised endurance 40 minutes or 35 minutes hovering depends on conditions.
3.26-inch 854×480 OLED display and 5,000 mAh controller battery; these belong to the ground controller, not the aircraft.
Autel Explorer for Android and iOS.

20 MP one-inch CMOS, 29 mm-equivalent f/2.8–f/11 lens. GPS/Galileo/BeiDou/GLONASS; manual identifies IMU, compass, barometer and visual positioning.

6.4-inch OLED; HDMI up to 1080p60, USB-A 2.0 and USB-C charging. Controller Wi-Fi 802.11a/b/g/n/ac and Bluetooth 5.0 do not establish those interfaces on the aircraft.

profiles.configuration: senseFly eBee X series user manual, manufacturer document hosted by its surveying distributor. Battery, camera and license affect configuration. Autopilot CPU, memory, GNSS chipset and radio-module SKU not named.

GNSS/RTK antenna, pitot airspeed probe, ambient-temperature sensor and downward LiDAR ground-distance sensor. Camera is interchangeable and powered by the aircraft battery.

1.16 m wingspan, 1.6 kg maximum takeoff mass and 300 g maximum camera payload. USB supports firmware updates and log retrieval.
eMotion flight planning and monitoring; RTK/PPK features depend on the applicable license.

profiles.configuration: Public P550 sheet version 250422. Payloads, datalinks and control systems are modular options. CPU, GPU, memory, radio part numbers and battery energy are not disclosed.

Battery-electric propulsion with hot-swappable batteries. Manufacturer advertises approximately five hours depending on configuration; battery voltage and capacity unspecified.
Tool-free connections and up to 6.8 kg mission payload, within 24.9 kg maximum gross takeoff mass. MOSA architecture supports third-party payloads and radios.
AVACORE/SPOTR-EDGE; baseline Vigilant Spirit with Quattro STANAG 4586. The 2025 sheet labels Kinesis GCS as future capability, not an installed baseline.

facts.details: Enhanced DDL with AES-256; 20 km standard, 40 km with ERA and 60 km with LRTA. Frequency is configuration-dependent and unspecified in this sheet.
GPS/INS module. Mantis i45 EO/IR payload or i45 N with dual LWIR and 5 MP low-light imaging. Visual Navigation System is an optional add-on.
Battery-powered motor/propeller and servo modules are field-replaceable. Standard ISR configuration is advertised at three hours; payload and battery selection change endurance.
Separate replaceable avionics, GPS/INS, DDL, payload, motor, servo and battery assemblies. Hand launch and deep-stall recovery; bungee launcher, VTOL kit and universal transit bay are optional.
Tomahawk, Crysalis or legacy ground-control systems. Ground computers are distinct from the aircraft’s undisclosed avionics processor.

profiles.configuration: A200-XT brochure configuration with a 2 km link; other Asteria publications describe different mission packages. CPU, memory, radio module/band, battery capacity and obstacle-sensor SKU undisclosed.

facts.details: Digital link with AES-128 encryption; brochure advertises up to 2 km. Frequency and modulation are not specified.

Dual-redundant GPS and omnidirectional obstacle sensing. Quick-connect options include HawkEye-4K, HawkEye-10T, HawkEye Night, HawkEye Dual, Cartis-MS and Cartis Surveyor Plus; they are alternative mission packages.
Battery-powered platform with low-battery failsafe; up to 40 minutes advertised. Battery voltage, energy and motor model are not published.
Tool-free assembly and swappable payload connections; 2.6 kg all-up weight in the brochure configuration.
Asteria MCS handles mission planning, payload control, video and recording. Automated takeoff/landing, geofencing and return-to-launch functions.

profiles.configuration: Commercial B2 cleaning configuration; separate from Blue/NDAA, spray-painting and NDT variants. CPU, memory, radio, battery capacity and sensor part numbers are not disclosed.

facts.details: Front obstacle detection and front distance hold. The B2 table does not establish the Blue variant’s additional side sensors.
Battery-powered drone; supplied system includes eight batteries and two chargers, not eight batteries installed simultaneously. Cleaning fluid comes through external hoses and pumps.

Compatible with standard nozzles, hoses and pumps. Published pump-side pressure up to 4,000 psi, flow up to 11 US gpm, and working height up to 60 m; these are configuration-dependent cleaning ratings.
21.5 lb without batteries, 25 lb payload rating and 55 lb all-up weight class. Extensions and soft-wash hose included; light bar, parachute and ball valve optional.
Apellix Intelligence Premium autonomous-cleaning software is listed as an optional add-on on the product page.

profiles.configuration: Architecture described directly by AMP founder Matanya Horowitz in January 2021. Not a parts list for later Cortex-C or Delta variants. CPU/GPU SKU, memory, electrical supply and radio hardware not identified.

facts.details: Color-camera imagery is processed by a GPU using a neural network; GPU manufacturer and model are not given.
Upstream color camera identifies items for sorting; camera and lens models unspecified.
Robot receives decisions from the vision system and places material into existing chutes or bins. The conveyor-mounted mechanism operates inside a safety enclosure.
Subscription services provide neural-network updates and business-intelligence reporting. No specific networking protocol or public scanner signature is established.

profiles.configuration: 2024 Delta Compact datasheet; not a specification for the standard Delta, Tandem or historical Cortex. CPU/GPU, RAM, storage and camera part numbers unspecified.

facts.details: AMP Vision imagery is classified by AMP AI, which directs the sorting robot. Exact camera and accelerator hardware are not published.
200–240 V AC, single phase, 50–60 Hz, 30 A breaker; 16 A average current. Air supply: 60 CFM at 120 psi, ISO 4.4.4.
IEEE 802.3 Ethernet, CAT5 or better; recommended internet upload 10 Mbps plus 1 Mbps per added unit, download 30 Mbps. Control-cabinet touchscreen: 23 inches.

profiles.configuration: Original SmartPower Brokk 170, not the later 170+ generation. Remotely operated demolition machine; no autonomous-navigation capability is established. CPU, memory, sensor and radio-chip part numbers unpublished.

Digital professional-radio connection or cable; advertised radio range up to 300 m. Frequency and packet format are not specified.

85 L hydraulic system, variable load-sensing pump, 18 MPa system pressure and 23 MPa attachment pressure. Pump flow 69/83 L/min at 50/60 Hz; tracked travel up to 2.1 km/h.
1,600 kg machine excluding options/tool; recommended attachment mass 270 kg. Hydraulic tools, cooling and CAN cable connection are configuration options.

profiles.configuration: Shared i-series arm architecture from the current hardware manual. Individual i3/i5/i7/i10/i12/i20 payloads, geometry and controllers differ; this family record does not assign one model’s ratings to all arms. CPU and memory undisclosed.

facts.details: Six articulated joints move the end tool under controller commands. Controller hardware and supplied package must be identified separately.
Joint motors and holding brakes maintain arm posture when power is removed; power demand depends on model and program.

facts.details: AUBO-CB-M control cabinet and AUBO-TP teach pendant; arm is a six-axis manipulator. No processor SKU is identified.
5 kg payload, 886.5 mm reach, 24 kg arm; typical 200 W and 2,000 W peak. Cabinet input 100–240 V AC, 50–60 Hz.
Ethernet, Modbus RTU/TCP and optional Profinet; tool RS485 and power connector. Cabinet 24 V/3 A I/O supply; tool selectable 0/12/24 V, 0.8 A.
USB supports updates and project import/export. CB-M manual lists 32 digital inputs and outputs, four analog inputs and outputs; safety and general channels have separate configuration.
SDK for C/C++/C#/Lua/Python, ROS support and API. Wired fieldbus support does not establish a Wi-Fi/BLE broadcast signature.

profiles.configuration: Single Conveyor configuration used as a reference for the unspecific MAG 1500 record; Lifter, Tugger and Fork versions differ. CPU, radio module and operating system unpublished. Camera part designation in the sheet needs manufacturer clarification.

facts.details: Manufacturer specifies a high-performance computer without a CPU SKU.
16 GB RAM and 64 GB SSD.

Two front/rear 2D safety LiDARs, two mechanical bumpers and four emergency-stop buttons. Sheet literally names an Intel D345i 3D camera; this designation is unresolved and is not silently changed to D435i.
48 V, 70 Ah LiFePO4 battery; advertised 9–10 hours runtime and 2–3 hours charging. Dual-spring suspension, on-spot turning; 1.4 m/s unloaded, 1.2 m/s loaded.
1,500 kg payload; 550 kg includes 350 kg base and 200 kg conveyor. Two RJ45 GbE, two USB 3.1, six GPIO and manual charge connection; 4.3-inch 800×480 HMI.

profiles.configuration: AES-incubated Maximo solar-construction platform; publications span generations, with the current company site naming Max 4.0. CPU/GPU SKU, RAM, radio hardware, battery ratings and sensor part numbers remain unpublished.

facts.details: AES describes onboard computation for vision, alignment and module placement; no processor part number is supplied. A processor illustration alone is not a hardware assignment.
Computer vision checks placement and corrects inconsistencies; safety sensing includes people detection and collision avoidance. Camera and safety-sensor SKUs are not identified.
Battery charge is monitored by the operator interface; AES describes a mobile microgrid supporting extended field shifts. Pack voltage, energy and propulsion topology are unspecified.
Mobile robotic module handling, placement and fastening; tooling compatibility is validated for specific module, clamp, rail and tracker combinations.

Current Maximo architecture names Cortex vision/planning, Form robots/tooling and MaxIQ fleet-performance software with a training-data feedback loop. These software layers do not identify a unique radio signature.

profiles.configuration: Architecture-level reference, not one universal truck bill of materials. Sensor ranges and compute change by generation. CPU/GPU models, memory, radio modules and their frequencies are not established by these documents.

facts.details: Main driving computer plus a separate fallback computer; fault-management software monitors hardware/software health and can transfer control after a failure.
Overlapping cameras, proprietary FirstLight LiDAR and imaging radar form pods adapted to each vehicle installation.
2021 safety report describes a central hardware hub conditioning/distributing its own power and synchronizing the sensors; vehicle and revision determine electrical ratings.
2021 report describes an umbilical linking the self-driving hardware to the vehicle. Physical connector and bus assignments are not published there.
Perception, planning and driving software work with fault-management and fallback systems. Current FAQ describes Aurora’s Verifiable AI approach.

profiles.configuration: Documented 2022 development-fleet hardware reference. Later commercial trucks can have different components; this does not apply the 2026 International LT kit to Peterbilt. CPU/GPU, memory, radio and engine configuration unspecified.

facts.details: Q3 2022 shareholder letter describes dual-lane liquid-cooled computers with redundant processing, self-health monitoring and fallback capability on its new Peterbilt 579 fleet.
FirstLight FMCW LiDAR with health reporting, integrated liquid cooling and cleaning. Upgraded camera system is illustrated as 8 MP with 32-bit HDR, versus prior 2 MP/24-bit imagery.
Peterbilt identifies its Model 579 as the host truck and distinguishes its 15-inch driver dashboard from the Aurora autonomy hardware.
The Q3 2022 letter reports Aurora Driver Beta 4.0 and fault-management/fallback development. This is historical hardware/software evidence, not a current fleet-version assertion.

profiles.configuration: July 2026 International LT launch and second-generation commercial hardware kit. Exact CPU/GPU, memory, radio, truck powertrain and battery configurations are not disclosed; do not substitute announced future-generation silicon.

facts.details: Aurora reports a more efficient onboard computer in the second-generation commercial kit; no silicon model or memory size is specified.
Proprietary long-range FMCW LiDAR with an advertised one-kilometer range for this kit; the range is not assigned to older Peterbilt hardware.
Second-generation driverless hardware is integrated with the International LT Series vehicle; the kit is engineered for one million miles of operation.
Aurora Driver operates the vehicle without a person in the driving seat in this launch configuration. An occasional roadside-assistance rider is described separately from the driving system.

profiles.configuration: Gen5 configuration described by NVIDIA and onsemi in 2021. Generic AutoX records must not be assumed to use Gen5. CPU, GPU board SKU, memory, powertrain and communications modules remain unspecified.

facts.details: NVIDIA identifies two Ampere-architecture GPUs, quoting 900 TOPS for that compute core and 2,200 TOPS for the overall Gen5 platform. These are distinct claims, not interchangeable processor ratings.
onsemi identifies 28 AR0820AT 8 MP image sensors and four SiPM arrays supplied for LiDAR. Four supplied arrays are not the total vehicle LiDAR count.
NVIDIA describes 28 cameras, six high-resolution LiDAR units and surround 4D millimeter-wave radar for the Gen5 system.
NVIDIA DRIVE-based computing runs autonomous-driving neural networks with capacity reserved for upgrades; the cited sources do not establish a Wi-Fi/BLE identification pattern.

profiles.configuration: Baidu’s July 2022 unveiling specification. Later RT6 production revisions may differ; no chipset, RAM, radio-module, battery-capacity or sensor-SKU assignment is made.

facts.details: Dual automotive-grade computing units with advertised aggregate performance up to 1,200 TOPS; main/backup architecture, processor models unspecified.
38 sensors, including eight LiDARs and twelve cameras, in the 2022 specification. Remaining sensor types are not itemized in the English release.
Purpose-built battery-electric vehicle on Baidu’s Xinghe electrical/electronic architecture, rather than a conventional-car retrofit. Motor and battery details are not supplied.
Detachable steering-wheel design, electric sliding doors and passenger interaction system; 4,760 mm length and 2,830 mm wheelbase.
Baidu describes redundant hardware/software plus integrated vehicle/autonomy fault diagnosis and risk-degradation handling.

profiles.configuration: Avride’s published Universal Driver sensor arrangement, associated with its documented Ioniq 5 fleet. Individual vehicles and revisions may differ. Processor SKU, RAM, storage, radio modules, battery trim and radar frequency unpublished.

facts.details: Specialized onboard computer described as comparable to server-grade hardware; exact CPU/GPU not named.
Five LiDARs, four radars and thirteen cameras. Proprietary central LiDAR: over 300 m range and 0.1-degree resolution; side LiDAR coverage within 50 m. Radars detect approaching vehicles up to 300 m.
Physical sensor-cleaning equipment and software filtering address precipitation, fog and other interference.
Nebius identifies Hyundai Ioniq 5 vehicles as the fleet platform supplied through Avride’s Hyundai partnership. Host-vehicle trim and battery pack are not specified.
LiDAR localization uses maintained 3D maps rather than GPS alone; fused perception feeds prediction and route/speed/trajectory planning.

profiles.configuration: Current Helium assessment configuration used as a reference for the generic Dax ADA record. Earlier Dax revisions differ. Exact Jetson module, RAM, storage, battery capacity and radio-module SKUs are not disclosed here.

facts.details: NVIDIA Jetson Orin for Mk III, with Xavier also listed for the platform. This does not identify every generation as Orin NX.
CTi TILT-57A dynamic inclinometer and three synchronized Keyence IL-300 lasers measure sidewalk slopes and defects.
RTK GPS plus tread-based odometry; stereo vision supports 3D mesh reconstruction.
5G, LTE and Wi-Fi; modem models and frequency/channel assignments unspecified.
50 kg; 6 km/h cruise; advertised 8–12 hours per charge with wireless charging through mobile Dax Hubs.
ArcGIS-compatible outputs combine georeferenced defects with stereo-derived 3D geometry.

profiles.configuration: Aetina’s 2024 Dax case-study configuration, separate from other Helium revisions. The head computer is identified; exact robot battery, radio chips and storage as installed are not established.

facts.details: Aetina AIB-MN32 platform with NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX, advertised up to 70 TOPS in this configuration.
Jetson Orin NX 8 GB. The board listing includes a 128 GB NVMe drive; the case study does not independently establish the robot’s installed drive.
Stereo cameras with IR filters/floodlight, stereo microphones, RTK GPS, laser measurement and an inclinometer; component SKUs unspecified in this case study.
LTE and Wi-Fi support dispatch, notifications and app interactions. No unique over-the-air identifier is established.
Customized audio board and speaker; AIB-MN32 reference lists two GbE ports and M.2 expansion. External accessibility on the robot is not documented.
DaxOS integrates vision and language tasks; case study names CUDA, Argus NvRaw and VPI. DaxOS software “chips” are not a count of physical processors.

profiles.configuration: Security-patrol Helium configuration, distinct from the ADA measurement robot. Exact Jetson SKU, RAM, storage, battery capacity and radio module are unpublished.

facts.details: NVIDIA Jetson Orin (Mk III) / Xavier, depending on revision.
Two Sony IMX678 camera modules, IR LED array and controlled IR-cut filter; electret-condenser microphones and two-way audio.
5G, LTE and Wi-Fi; no band or device-specific broadcast pattern published.
50 kg tracked robot, 6 km/h cruise and advertised 8–10 hours per charge; wireless charging at Dax Huts.
700-lumen spotlight and audio output support remote interaction.

profiles.configuration: V2 operations-manual configuration used as a qualified reference for generic Pro records; not Evo or original V1 hardware. Flight-controller and companion-computer processor SKUs, RAM and radio modules remain unspecified.

facts.details: Flight controller plus a secondary onboard computer serving payload integration. Neither processor is named.
Flight controller records logs to an SD card; capacity is unspecified.
Radio telemetry or optional USB 4G dongle in the aircraft nose. MAVLink can traverse the configured ZeroTier VPN; ground-station hotspot instructions do not establish an aircraft Wi-Fi radio.
Compass, gyroscope and accelerometer calibration; GPS connection. ADS-B receiver and ruggedized GPS are optional wiring configurations.
Four lift motors and a pusher motor; 4S 23 Ah LiPo, 6.2 kg MTOW and 1.2 kg maximum payload. Auxiliary-battery endurance figures describe a different payload configuration.
SBUS radio input, PWM motors/wing servos and telemetry UARTs; optional camera triggers or payload-release mechanism. Connections depend on fitted options.
PX4-based vehicle firmware and QGroundControl mission/maintenance interface.

profiles.configuration: August 2021 Commander2 specification, not the original Commander or Commander 3 XL. CPU, RAM, storage, radio module/band and battery capacity are not supplied.

facts.details: Manufacturer describes a new North American-sourced flight controller without naming its processor.
Encrypted radio communications and real-time video for compatible payloads; air protocol and frequency unspecified.
Optional PPK/RTK GPS and base station. Interchangeable payload choices include FLIR Duo Pro R 640, MicaSense RedEdge MX with DLS2, 24 MP RGB and 10× zoom cameras; these are alternatives.
Dual-battery system; 2.75 kg with batteries, 3.75 kg MTOW and 1 kg payload. Typical flight time is 30 minutes with payload.
Quickly interchangeable gimballed camera packages; customized sensor integration offered separately.
MAVLink-based mission planning supports automatic, semi-automatic and manual operation.

profiles.configuration: Battery-electric Commander 3 XL: current controller/radio options plus a separately dated 2022 physical specification. Not the Hybrid. Exact Cube variant, CPU, RAM and battery energy are unspecified.

facts.details: Cube autopilot with triple-redundant IMU; the product page does not name a Cube color/version or processor SKU.
Microhard PDDL, Herelink Blue, Doodle Labs Helix or DTC BluSDR. These are alternative configurations, not four simultaneously installed radios; exact frequency SKUs need configuration records.
Triple IMU; optional Gremsy VIO payload combines 4K zoom, 640×512 radiometric thermal imaging and a 2,400 m laser rangefinder.
2022 sheet specifies 55 lb MTOW, 29 lb including batteries, 22 lb payload and up to 50 minutes flight. Endurance depends on payload and conditions.
Quick-detach arms, retractable landing gear and universal payload mounting support interchangeable camera and delivery equipment.

profiles.configuration: September 2023 target specification, explicitly subject to change. No controller, compute, memory, radio or sensor BOM is established; battery-electric Commander 3 XL components are not inherited.

facts.details: Pegasus-powered Draganfuel Ignite 70 cc two-stroke, fuel-injected and liquid-cooled engine-generator; 4 kW maximum, 2–3.5 kW ideal output, 24–50 V.
25 kg MTOW, 4 kg maximum payload; advertised target endurance up to three hours. Generator base mass is 3.5 kg, not total aircraft mass.
Automatic throttle and self-starting engine with capacitive-discharge ignition. The sheet does not identify an external control bus.

profiles.configuration: Iris family architecture, not one universal payload. CPU, RAM, storage, radio hardware and propulsion/battery specifications are unpublished in these sources.

facts.details: Onboard laser positioning, obstacle detection and automatically controlled camera gimbal; external positioning beacons are not required.
Tablet starts the automated inspection flight; sensor payload differs by Iris variant.
Captured imagery passes to analysis software and maintenance reports; Donecle cloud stores inspection history and supports team access.
Iris GVI performs visual inspection; Iris dentCHECK uses a separate 3D measurement payload. Neither payload is assigned to every Iris.

profiles.configuration: GVI visual-inspection configuration. Processor, memory, battery and radio-module details remain unpublished.

facts.details: 24 MP camera, advertised 16 pixels/mm² inspection resolution; image-sensor manufacturer/model unspecified.
Iris laser-based localization operates without GPS or external beacons, with obstacle detection and automatic gimbal control.
Tablet-based mission launch; image analysis and report review remain separate workflow stages.
Inspection results enter Donecle’s analysis/reporting and cloud history platform.

profiles.configuration: 3D dent-measurement configuration, separate from GVI. CPU, memory, radio and power-system details remain unpublished.

facts.details: 8tree dentCHECK sensor measures surface dents and buckles; advertised depth accuracy 0.1 mm. This is not the GVI camera specification.
Iris laser localization and obstacle detection support automated scanning around the inspected structure.
Measurements support digitized dent maps and reports for specified aircraft surfaces; supported airframes and operational approval depend on configuration.

profiles.configuration: 557 MPA reference for the generic Robot 557 record; other 557 variants can differ. Automated concrete removal does not establish autonomous road navigation. CPU, memory and radio-chip identifiers are unpublished.

facts.details: ConjetONE control system, configurable through radio handset or onboard display; controller CPU unspecified.
Remote radio control; an optional wireless kit links robot and pump controls. Frequencies and protocols are not published.
18.7 kW diesel or three-phase electric supply: 380–480 V AC/32 A, alternatively 200 V AC/63 A, 50–60 Hz.
2,740 kg; tracks extend from 1,200 to 1,900 mm and main body slides 400 mm for stability. Multipurpose arm reaches 5.05 m vertically.
Hydrodemolition tool kits and high-pressure pumps; prepared for Conjet Connect, which is not proof that every robot has a connected subscription.

profiles.configuration: Second-generation survey AUV, using the 2024 manufacturer sheet and a direct CTO interview. Exact processor-board revision, memory, storage and radio modules remain unspecified; payload configurations differ.

facts.details: CEO/CTO Charles Chiau identifies NVIDIA Jetson TX2 as the primary GPU solution in the interviewed vehicle configuration.
Exail Phins 9 Compact INS, Nortek DVL500/DVL1000 Compact listed options, and u-blox ZED-F9P-02B L1/L2 GNSS.
NORBIT FLS-42 forward sonar; AML pressure and sound-velocity/temperature sensors. SonTek Castaway CTD is deployed from the support vessel, not onboard.
Configuration 1: NORBIT MBES-42, Starfish 454 and OFG magnetometer. Configuration 2: NORBIT SBP-42, Starfish 992 and OFG magnetometer. Sonar frequencies describe acoustic signals, not radio bands.
Iridium, Wi-Fi, ISM radios and acoustic communications; independent acoustic recovery tracker. Exact radio bands unspecified.
Swappable 3 kWh lithium-ion battery; 2.4 m, 60 kg, 300 m depth rating and 3-knot survey speed.
Onboard quality-control processing, Trident operational control and Mosaic survey-data platform; these cloud products do not imply a public live location feed.

profiles.configuration: February 2026 long-range multi-use PF4 specification. This is not PF4-CAT3. CPU, RAM, storage, modem SKU and battery voltage/chemistry are not disclosed in this release.

facts.details: 2.4 GHz link advertised to 4 km unobstructed, or LTE within coverage; multi-SIM is optional.
GPS plus QZSS, CLAS-compatible. Optional mission payloads include YellowScan Ultra 3+ LiDAR, VIO infrared/visible camera and CX-GB200 gimbal camera.
Four 20,000 mAh batteries; 12.1 kg airframe and 19.4 kg with batteries in logistics configuration. Maximum payload 5.5 kg; advertised endurance 70 minutes empty or 50 minutes loaded.
User-exchangeable payloads, hot-swap capability and remote controller. Electrical connector details are not given.

profiles.configuration: June 2024 logistics-aircraft development/type-certificate application specification, formerly JP2. An application is not a granted certificate. CPU, memory, radio, navigation sensors and battery remain undisclosed; PF4 multi-use specifications are not substituted.

facts.details: Approximately 2.3 × 2.5 × 0.6 m, 24.9 kg MTOW and 5 kg payload; development reference range approximately 35 km.
Cargo enters through the top of the aircraft and detaches from the bottom.

profiles.configuration: Historical 2013 Command architecture reference. Later kits and jurisdictions differ. CPU, RAM and radio-chip SKUs are undisclosed; these frequencies are not universal identifiers for all Cat machines.

facts.details: Dual GNSS receivers, object-detection sensors, machine-health and tire/payload monitoring. Specification lists 76.5 GHz radar and 64-beam rotating LiDAR.
Wireless exchange with MineStar and nearby machines; separately documented A-stop transmitter at 919 MHz. The latter is a historical configuration-specific frequency.
Display and onboard A-stop receiver accept 9–32 V DC; radar is rated 12 V, 1 A. These are electronics ratings, not vehicle propulsion power.
6.5-inch 640×480 touch display with four NTSC video inputs; GNSS receiver uses a 12-pin Deutsch connector and TNC antenna connection.
MineStar coordinates mapped autonomous operating areas, fleet assignments and diagnostics.

profiles.configuration: 793F host truck with Command compatibility. Host powertrain and historical Command architecture are separately sourced; sensor/radio revisions on any deployed truck require its configuration records. CPU and memory unpublished.

facts.details: Cat C175-16 diesel, rated 1,976 kW gross in this brochure, driving a six-speed mechanical powershift transmission; this is not the newer unsuffixed 793.
VIMS monitoring and service data interface support diagnostics; exact autonomous-kit connectors are unspecified.
Caterpillar explicitly lists the 793F among models supporting Command for hauling retrofit kits.
2013 architecture uses dual GNSS and obstacle sensors. This does not establish the sensor SKU installed on a later 793F.

profiles.configuration: 789D mining-truck host and documented Command retrofit compatibility, not the separate autonomous water-truck equipment package. Exact autonomous CPU, sensors, modem and memory are unpublished here.

facts.details: 3516C-HD diesel rated 1,566 kW gross, or optional 3516B EUI rated 1,417 kW. Engines are alternatives rather than interchangeable specifications.
Six forward powershift gears with mechanical final drives; payload and gross-weight limits depend on body/tire configuration.
VIMS machine monitoring and service connections; controller silicon not named.
Caterpillar lists 789D among trucks supporting Command for hauling retrofit kits. This establishes platform compatibility, not a universal sensor or radio BOM.

profiles.configuration: Current hardware reference; Devanthro reports several generations since 2023. Exact Orin variant, RAM, storage, battery capacity and radio-module identifiers are unspecified.

facts.details: NVIDIA Jetson Orin plus Orin Nano; the larger Orin module is not identified as AGX or NX.
4K fisheye RGB cameras, millimeter-wave radar and stereo microphones; sensor SKUs and radar frequency unspecified.
Differential-drive base; 60 kg, 1.65 m tall; advertised six-hour operation and self-docking.
QDD and Dynamixel actuators; two 6-DOF arms with 1.5 kg payload each, two-finger grippers and a 3-DOF neck.
ROS 2 middleware with human-in-the-loop VR telepresence and stereoscopic video. This configuration is not described as fully autonomous.

profiles.configuration: 2026 Mech platform and supplier-disclosed control architecture. The lower-level controller is separate from the AI computer; AI accelerator, installed memory/storage, radio and battery capacity remain unspecified.

facts.details: Beckhoff CX5240 with Intel Atom x5-E3940 handles motion and safety logic. It is not identified as the robot’s AI inference computer.
Beckhoff EP3751-0260 EtherCAT box supplies accelerometer and gyroscope measurements.
Up to sixteen cameras; arm torque control operates at 4 kHz. Camera SKUs are not disclosed.
Battery-powered rover with four steerable wheels and dual vacuum pumps; two Kawasaki-manufactured arms, HiWin motion components, 60 kg combined lift and 5.4 m armspan.
EtherCAT and CAN, PCB-mounted Beckhoff EJ-series I/O and TwinSAFE functional safety. Generic wireless EtherCAT capability does not establish an installed RF module.
Windows 10 IoT Enterprise on the CX5240; Dexterity Physical AI supplies higher-level decisions and can operate standalone or with cloud services.

profiles.configuration: DexR trailer-loading robot in Dexterity’s September 2023 announcement. This does not establish the later Mech hardware BOM; CPU, memory, radios, battery and camera SKUs are unpublished.

facts.details: Vision builds a 3D representation of boxes and trailer space; force control supplies contact feedback while packing.
Autonomous mobile base docks to a powered conveyor; two arms can pick and place boxes concurrently.
Integrated motion planning coordinates both arms; packing software updates the trailer model as boxes arrive and learns from completed placements.

profiles.configuration: October 2026 Developer/Pro manual configuration, offered as a dated reference for generic T800 records. It differs from the retail edition table; do not combine its NEZHA/Odin2/battery specifications with the retail Basic edition.

facts.details: Four-core NEZHA Robot PC, called NeZha N97 in the interface table, plus a twelve-core NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin AI PC.
Robot PC: 8 GB RAM and 64 GB storage. AI PC: 64 GB RAM and 256 GB SSD.
Odin2 head module integrates stereo RGB, LiDAR and IMU over Gigabit Ethernet; two SC132GS global-shutter image sensors and 940 nm optical ranging.
Torso IMU documentation lists Yesense YIS320-E11 UART / YIS320-E30 USB alternatives. Four microphones and two speakers; Pro adds five tactile sensors per hand.
Network diagram places Wi-Fi on the application computer; radio chipset and band are unspecified in this manual.
Removable ternary-lithium battery: 61.2 V, 20 Ah, 1.22 kWh; charged outside the robot. This is not evidence of the retail page’s advertised solid-state battery chemistry.
Developer: 25 DOF, approximately 84.5 kg. Pro: 29 body DOF plus fourteen hand DOF, approximately 85.3 kg; 1.73 m tall.
Both computers connect by Ethernet to an onboard router. External RJ45 plus separate USB-A 3.0 connections to the Orin and NEZHA computers.
Ubuntu on both computers; ROS 2 interfaces expose motion and sensor topics for authorized development.

profiles.configuration: Retail comparison read November 2026. These edition specifications differ from the October developer manual; no equivalence between its NEZHA controller and the retail eight-core CPU is established.

facts.details: Basic: Orin NX 16G. Open Source, Pro and Max: AGX Orin 64G, with Thor offered on request. All list an unnamed eight-core base CPU.
Basic: 16 GB; higher editions: 64 GB. Installed storage is not listed.
Basic lists an Intel binocular camera and no 3D LiDAR. Open Source, Pro and Max list binocular cameras plus LiDAR; sensor SKUs unspecified.
Wi-Fi 5 and Bluetooth 5.0 throughout; Max additionally lists 5G. These are shared standards, not unique robot identifiers.
Basic/Open Source: 25 DOF. Pro: 43 including hands. Max: 46 including hands and a three-axis waist.
Quick-removal lithium battery; capacity not established by the retail table.

profiles.configuration: Current SE01 product-page hardware reference. No exact CPU/GPU, RAM, radio, battery capacity or sensor part numbers are established; T800 components are not inherited.

facts.details: LiDAR, depth and infrared cameras; body diagram labels RGB-D, an IMU and high-precision force sensors.
Removable battery with power-management system; proprietary planetary, harmonic and linear joint actuators. The page’s ambiguous battery-capacity display is not used as a rating.
Gigabit Ethernet and USB 3.0; six-DOF dexterous hand with force feedback, plus two speakers.

profiles.configuration: 620 S G2 / TS4.2 manual configuration used as a qualified ARA reference. This is a tractor-mounted precision sprayer, not a self-driving tractor. Exact CPU/GPU, RAM, storage and modem parts remain unspecified.

facts.details: Six vision boxes each contain an image-processing computer, LED-control board and cooling fan; processor models are not named.
Each box has a target-recognition camera, four flash LEDs and a visual-odometry camera; a boom pressure sensor feeds one vision computer.
Router and switch in the main electrical box, with Wi-Fi and 4G antenna. Radio bands, MAC allocations and modem SKU are not established.
Two 12 V lead batteries in series provide 24 V; a PTO-driven 28 V alternator recharges them. Vision boxes have RTC backup batteries.
Three master vision boxes drive solenoid valves across three booms; remote on/off and boom-height controls.
156 Euspray OC1X502 nozzles, 152 effective with all three booms; 6.04 m effective spray width and 10 ms minimum valve opening.
Target recognition and visual odometry time nozzle activation to the machine’s forward motion.

profiles.configuration: Current modular H6 family. Generic records do not identify the fitted powertrain; Electric, Hybrid EFI and Hydrone configurations are documented separately. Processor silicon, RAM and storage are not identified here.

facts.details: Shared folding hexacopter airframe accepts battery-electric, gasoline/EFI hybrid or hydrogen fuel-cell systems; these are alternatives.
Platform specification lists triple-redundant IMU and dual RTK GNSS; sensor part numbers unspecified.
UART, Ethernet, CAN, USB and GPIO with 12/24/48 V payload power; payload sensors are selectable.

profiles.configuration: Current manufacturer specification, separate from older H6 datasheets and other powertrains. Exact processor silicon, RAM, storage and RF-module SKU are unspecified; receiver-only ADS-B does not make this aircraft an ADS-B transmitter.

facts.details: Cube Orange+ running a customized ArduPilot stack.
2.4 GHz ISM and 902–928 MHz; configured hardware and regional permissions determine the fitted band.
Triple-redundant IMU and ADS-B receiver; camera/LiDAR payloads are optional integrations.
Two parallel 12S1P 16,000 mAh LiPo packs: 44.4 V nominal, 32 Ah combined; AS150U-F connector. Six KV100-equivalent motors and 29.2 × 9.2-inch propellers.
UART, Ethernet, CAN, GPIO and USB; regulated 5/12/24/48 V outputs. Ground-control choices include C-GCS, C-NAV, C-SRoC or HereLink.

profiles.configuration: Current manufacturer specification, separate from older H6 datasheets and other powertrains. Exact processor silicon, RAM, storage and RF-module SKU are unspecified; receiver-only ADS-B does not make this aircraft an ADS-B transmitter.

facts.details: Cube Orange+ running a customized ArduPilot stack.
2.4 GHz ISM and 902–928 MHz; configured hardware and regional permissions determine the fitted band.
Triple-redundant IMU and ADS-B receiver; camera/LiDAR payloads are optional integrations.
H2400 EFI two-stroke gasoline generator, 2.4 kW continuous, 6.5 L tank; two 6S1P LiPo backup packs provide a stated five-minute reserve.
UART, Ethernet, CAN, GPIO and USB; regulated 5/12/24/48 V outputs. Ground-control choices include C-GCS, C-NAV, C-SRoC or HereLink.

profiles.configuration: Current manufacturer specification, separate from older H6 datasheets and other powertrains. Exact processor silicon, RAM, storage and RF-module SKU are unspecified; receiver-only ADS-B does not make this aircraft an ADS-B transmitter.

facts.details: Cube Orange+ running a customized ArduPilot stack.
2.4 GHz ISM and 902–928 MHz; configured hardware and regional permissions determine the fitted band.
Triple-redundant IMU and ADS-B receiver; camera/LiDAR payloads are optional integrations.
2.4 kW hydrogen fuel-cell module, 10.8 L / 350-bar cylinder and 6S2P LiPo backup. Fuel-cell and battery reserves depend on configuration.
UART, Ethernet, CAN, GPIO and USB; regulated 5/12/24/48 V outputs. Ground-control choices include C-GCS, C-NAV, C-SRoC or HereLink.

profiles.configuration: Legacy H8E identified explicitly in Harris support documentation; not the newer HX8. Family-wide service guidance is qualified below. CPU, Cube revision, battery capacity, RAM and storage capacity are not established.

facts.details: H8E calibration instructions identify compass and IMU/accelerometer, with GPS checked before flight.
H8E setup uses USB or telemetry with Mission Planner. General Carrier guidance locates flight logs on an SD card beside the Cube autopilot; the exact H8E controller revision is not given.
Support documentation describes RF Design 900 MHz, Microhard 2.4 GHz and HereLink alternatives; the fitted radio must be established per aircraft.
Carrier service guide pairs Microhard with InVID Ethernet video and HereLink with CamPark mini-HDMI video; H8 camera mounting is explicitly discussed.
Support instructions form the Basic ID from 18136 + H8E + vehicle serial. This is a configured serial template, not a MAC address or proof of nearby reception.

profiles.configuration: Current FB3 cargo-platform reference. Flight controller, CPU, memory, radio chip/bands and battery voltage/capacity are unpublished. The page’s safety block names FB4, so its ADS-B/radar claims are not assigned to FB3.

facts.details: Eight propulsion units powered by four swappable lithium-ion battery packs; 70 kg empty mass and 100 kg maximum cargo.
RF plus 4G links are listed for the ground-control packages; exact air-interface protocols are not specified.
Essentials: seven-inch handheld GCS. Standard: ten-inch handheld GCS. Pro: three-screen mobile GCS. These are alternative kits.
Essentials includes a 7 kW single-phase charger; Standard/Pro include a 16 kW three-phase charger.
Air-and-ground Starlink C2 is offered for Standard and Pro kits, not Essentials.
Gimbal video in all three kits; additional FPV video in Pro. Camera models and resolutions unspecified.

profiles.configuration: G1 Quick Start Guide V2.0 in developer documentation 2.2.4. Component vendors beyond the compute module, installed storage and unique radio identifiers are not disclosed.

facts.details: NVIDIA AGX Orin, rated 275 TOPS.
64 GB; storage capacity unspecified.
2.4/5 GHz Wi-Fi and Bluetooth 5.2; shared standards do not identify a particular robot.
One head stereo camera; four torso RGB cameras and two torso IMUs; two wrist depth cameras and two six-axis wrist force sensors.
